input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. It bars assignment by either party absent the other's prior written approval, with the sole exception of an assignment to a "financially responsible affiliate." It therefore fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Client's assets would require TrueLink's consent — the playbook treats a Customer assignment restriction with no M&A carve-out as walk-away territory; and (ii) the consent standard is unqualified, not "not to be unreasonably withheld," so TrueLink may refuse arbitrarily (including on our affiliate transfers, where "financially responsible" is itself a judgment call). There is no competitor restriction on TrueLink's side. On the positive side, no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists anywhere in the document (searches for "change of control" and "merger" returned nothing, and the term/termination provisions at Sections 13-14 contain no such trigger), so only the assignment carve-outs need fixing. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, subjects TrueLink's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a Client competitor, and confirms that a Client change of control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no exit.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment rights for Client, reasonableness standard on Client consent, and confirm no Vendor exit on Client change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the customary affiliate and successor (merger/acquisition/sale of assets) carve-out so our internal reorganizations and M&A are not held up by consent, and made TrueLink's assignment subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor. We also confirmed that a change of control of Client is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right; if helpful, we can instead accept a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Client may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the prior approval of TrueLink, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written approval of Client, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of Client. Any other assignment by Client shall require the prior written approval of TrueLink, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld. No change of control of Client shall constitute an assignment or give TrueLink any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
